learningObjectives: Explain the structure of the Requirements hierarchy in Tosca (RequirementFolder → RequirementSet → Requirement).
Define how Requirement weights are calculated using frequency class and damage class.
Link TestCases to individual Requirements and ExecutionLists to the RequirementSet.
Use 'Update Outdated Values' to refresh coverage and execution status after linking.
Understand the relationship between Requirements and test coverage.

elements.description: Criteria the system under test (SUT) is expected to fulfill. They map business requirements to checks that confirm the application works properly.
items: Functional requirement — a functionality the SUT must carry out (e.g., 'the web shop must be able to process payments').
Non-functional requirement — a quality/operational attribute rather than a specific behavior (e.g., security, reliability, performance, maintainability, scalability, usability).

rows: Optional grouping that structures RequirementSets one level up
Represents an aspect of the app (e.g., 'Webshop Frontend'); organizes Requirements

elements.text: Two different link targets (confirmed by Exercise 22): TestCases link to individual Requirements (bottom level). The ExecutionList is dragged onto the RequirementSet (middle level, e.g., 'Webshop Frontend') — NOT onto an individual Requirement.

Think of a filing cabinet: RequirementFolder = the cabinet, RequirementSet = a drawer, Requirement = an individual document. You attach a TestCase sticky note to a specific document, but you register the whole ExecutionList against the drawer (the Set).

bulletPoints: Requirement types: functional (what the SUT must do) vs non-functional (security, performance, usability, etc.).
RequirementFolder is a level UP from RequirementSet — it groups Sets, not the other way around.
TestCase → individual Requirement. ExecutionList → RequirementSet. (Different targets.)

elements.description: A calculated risk score (integer 1–10) representing the priority and risk of a Requirement. Derived automatically by Tosca — not manually entered.
items: Input 1: Frequency Class — how often the failure occurs if the requirement is unmet
Input 2: Damage Class — the severity of the impact if the requirement fails
Formula: exponential function of (Frequency Class, Damage Class)
Output: integer from 1 (lowest risk) to 10 (highest risk)

elements.text: Weight is CALCULATED by Tosca from the two class inputs — it is not a field you type into directly. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.

bulletPoints: Higher weight = higher risk = higher test priority.
Frequency Class: how often? Damage Class: how bad? → Tosca calculates the weight.
Weight range: integer 1–10 (not 1–5, not a decimal).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Linking TestCases and ExecutionLists to Requirements

elements.description: Drag a COMPLETED TestCase onto an individual Requirement to create a link. This provides traceability: which tests cover which requirements. Link at the Requirement (atomic, bottom) level.
Drag an ExecutionList onto a RequirementSet to associate its execution results with that set of requirements — enabling execution/coverage reporting across the whole set.

After linking TestCases and ExecutionLists, right-click the RequirementSet and select 'Update Outdated Values' to refresh the calculated coverage and execution status. Without this, displayed values may be stale.
items: Right-click the RequirementSet (e.g., 'Webshop Frontend') → 'Update Outdated Values'.
Recalculates coverage and pulls in the latest execution results from linked ExecutionLists.
Run it whenever links change or new results come in.

elements.title: Linking workflow (Exercise 22 procedure):
items: Confirm the TestCases are COMPLETED and Business Parameters are entered.
In Requirements, expand the target RequirementSet (e.g., Webshop Frontend).
Drag each COMPLETED TestCase onto its matching individual Requirement.
In the Execution section, drag the ExecutionList onto the RequirementSet.
Right-click the RequirementSet → 'Update Outdated Values'. Save your work.

elements.description: Once TestCases are linked, Tosca shows requirement coverage — which requirements have linked tests (covered) and which do not (unverified).

bulletPoints: TestCase → individual Requirement. ExecutionList → RequirementSet. Different targets.
After linking, run 'Update Outdated Values' on the RequirementSet to refresh coverage/results.
Unlinked Requirements appear as gaps in the coverage report — find and cover them.

examPitfalls.title: TestCases link to Requirement — not RequirementSet or Folder
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Exam asks: 'To which level in the Requirement structure are TestCases linked?' Options include RequirementFolder, RequirementSet, and Requirement. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TestCases link to the individual Requirement — the most specific, atomic level. NOT to RequirementSet or RequirementFolder.

examPitfalls.title: ExecutionList links to the RequirementSet, not an individual Requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume ExecutionLists link at the same level as TestCases (the individual Requirement). In Exercise 22 the ExecutionList is dropped on the RequirementSet.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TestCase → individual Requirement (bottom level). ExecutionList → RequirementSet (middle level). They have DIFFERENT link targets.

examPitfalls.title: Hierarchy order — Folder is ABOVE Set
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates place RequirementSet above RequirementFolder. Distractors reverse the order.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Top-to-bottom: RequirementFolder → RequirementSet → Requirement. A RequirementFolder groups RequirementSets (a level up), not the reverse.

examPitfalls.title: Update Outdated Values must be run after linking
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates link TestCases/ExecutionLists but see stale coverage or execution status and think linking failed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: After linking, right-click the RequirementSet → 'Update Outdated Values' to recalculate coverage and pull in the latest execution results.

examPitfalls.title: Functional vs non-functional Requirements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates mislabel a performance/security criterion as functional.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Functional = what the SUT must DO (e.g., process payments). Non-functional = quality attributes of operation (security, performance, reliability, usability, scalability, maintainability).

examPitfalls.title: Weight formula — exponential, not integer sum
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume weight is simply frequency + damage, expressed as a simple sum or a scale from 1-5.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Weight is calculated via an exponential function from frequency class and damage class. Result is an integer from 1 to 10. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.

examPitfalls.title: Weight is not manually assigned
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think testers manually type in the weight value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Weight is CALCULATED by Tosca from the frequency and damage class inputs. It is derived, not directly entered.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How often can you use a TestCase in the same ExecutionList?

options.text: The number is set in the TestCase properties tab

practiceQuiz.hint: There is no cap on reuse.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestCase can be used an UNLIMITED number of times in the same ExecutionList. Each entry is an independent execution. This is a verbatim official Knowledge Check question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do we define the final weight of a Requirement?

options.text: It is expressed in integers ranging from 1 to 10
It is calculated using an exponential function that takes into consideration frequency class and damage class
It is expressed in integers ranging from 1 to 5
It is pre-defined based on the requirement complexity

practiceQuiz.hint: The question asks HOW it is defined (the method), not the value range.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The weight is DEFINED by an exponential function combining frequency class and damage class. Watch the trap: although the resulting value IS an integer from 1 to 10, the question asks how the weight is defined — so the method (exponential function) is the correct answer, not the range. Verbatim official Knowledge Check question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: To which level in the Requirement structure are TestCases linked?

options.text: TestCases are not linked to the Requirement section

practiceQuiz.rationale: TestCases link to the individual Requirement — the atomic, testable unit at the bottom of the hierarchy. Note: ExecutionLists link to the RequirementSet, but TestCases link to the Requirement. Verbatim official Knowledge Check question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In which section of Tosca are libraries used?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Libraries are used in the TestCase section — they store Reusable TestStepBlocks that other TestCases reference. NOT in Module, TestCaseDesign, or Requirements. Verbatim official Knowledge Check question (cross-topic, from Section 03).

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct syntax for using a Test Configuration Parameter in a TestStep?
practiceQuiz.hint: Outer curly braces, CP prefix, name in square brackets.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {CP[NameOfTheTCP]} is correct: outer curly braces are mandatory, CP is the prefix, and the name goes in square brackets. TCP is the wrong prefix. Verbatim official Knowledge Check question (cross-topic, from Sections 03/05).

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct expression, if you want Tosca to enter a date that is: the last day of the month, 3 years ago from the testing date, with 4 digits for years and 3 words abbreviation for month?
practiceQuiz.hint: MONTHLAST for the last day; -3y for 3 years ago; MMMyyyy for 3-letter month + 4-digit year.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {MONTHLAST[][-3y][MMMyyyy]} is correct: MONTHLAST = last day of month, [] = today as start, [-3y] = minus 3 years, [MMMyyyy] = 3-letter month abbreviation + 4-digit year. Verbatim official Knowledge Check question (cross-topic, from Section 03).

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test team wants to demonstrate that their ExecutionList covers a specific compliance requirement. What should they do?

options.text: Add the requirement text as a comment inside the ExecutionList.
Copy the Requirement into the ExecutionList description field.
Link the ExecutionList to the relevant Requirement in the Requirements section.
ExecutionLists cannot be linked to Requirements in Tosca.

practiceQuiz.hint: Tosca supports linking ExecutionLists to Requirements.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists can be linked to Requirements in Tosca, providing traceability from execution run to requirement. This enables formal compliance reporting and coverage analysis.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct hierarchy in the Requirements section of Tosca Commander, from top to bottom?
practiceQuiz.hint: A Folder groups Sets — so the Folder sits a level UP.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The hierarchy is RequirementFolder (top grouping) → RequirementSet (aspect of the app) → Requirement (individual, testable item). A RequirementFolder is a level up that structures RequirementSets. TestCases link to the individual Requirement at the bottom.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In Exercise 22, after linking the TestCases, where is the ExecutionList 'Web Shop' dragged and dropped?

options.text: Onto each individual Requirement, one at a time.
Onto the RequirementFolder at the very top.
ExecutionLists cannot be linked to Requirements.

practiceQuiz.hint: ExecutionLists and TestCases have different link targets.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The ExecutionList is dropped onto the RequirementSet ('Webshop Frontend'), while TestCases are linked to individual Requirements. TestCase → Requirement; ExecutionList → RequirementSet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After dragging TestCases and an ExecutionList to Requirements, the coverage and execution status shown still look outdated. What is the correct next step?

options.text: Right-click the RequirementSet and select 'Update Outdated Values'.
Re-run the entire ExecutionList from scratch.
Restart Tosca Commander to force a refresh.

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a dedicated right-click command to refresh values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Update Outdated Values' (right-click the RequirementSet) recalculates coverage and pulls in the latest execution results from linked ExecutionLists. This is the exact step 5 in Exercise 22.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following is a NON-functional requirement for an online web shop?

options.text: The shop must be able to process credit card payments.
The shop must let users add items to a cart.
The shop must load any product page within 2 seconds (performance).
The shop must calculate shipping costs.

practiceQuiz.hint: Non-functional = a quality attribute, not a specific behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Performance (page load within 2 seconds) is a non-functional requirement — it describes an operational quality attribute. Processing payments, adding to cart, and calculating shipping are functional requirements (specific behaviors the SUT must perform).

quickRecap.value: Functional = what the SUT must DO. Non-functional = quality attributes (security, performance, usability...).
RequirementFolder → RequirementSet → Requirement (top to bottom). Folder is a level UP from Set.
TestCases link to the individual Requirement (bottom, atomic level).
ExecutionLists link to the RequirementSet (middle level) — different target than TestCases.
Right-click the RequirementSet → 'Update Outdated Values' to refresh coverage & execution status after linking.
Exponential function of frequency class + damage class. Result: integer 1–10. Auto-calculated, not typed.
How often the failure occurs if the requirement is unmet.
Severity of impact if the requirement fails.
